All plots and printed diagnostics are left untouched.\",\n  \"export_code\": \"# --- Endpoint export: terminal scientific results ---\\n\\nimport os\\n\\nos.makedirs(\\\"/work/outputs\\\", exist_ok=True)\\n\\n# Final result of the tutorial: CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF, ENCODE ENCFF401MQL)\\n# each assigned the strongest overlapping JASPAR CTCF motif (MA0139.1), with\\n# peaks within +/-1kb of ENCODE blacklist regions (ENCFF356LFX) removed.\\n# Written as-is from the dataframe produced by bioframe.subtract above.\\ndf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.to_csv(\\n    \\\"/work/outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv\\\", index=False\\n)\",\n  \"unresolved_assumptions\": [\n    \"The final column set/order of df_peaks_maxmotif_clean is assumed to be chrom, start, end, fc, chrom_2, start_2, end_2, pval_2, strand_2 after the rename and subtract steps; confirm at execution.\",\n    \"Peaks with no overlapping motif retain NaN in pval_2 and empty motif coordinates; in CSV these appear as empty fields.\",\n    \"The inplace replace/rename chained-assignment patterns in the original script may warn or behave differently under the execution environment's pandas version; fidelity of the final-state table is a validation question, not something the export changes.\",\n    \"Remote retrieval of the ENCODE peaks, ENCODE blacklist and JASPAR motif files must succeed during the network-enabled setup stage; the offline reference run assumes those inputs are staged unchanged.\"\n  ]\n}\n",

  "specification": {
    "task_brief": "# Task: assign the strongest CTCF motif to each CTCF ChIP-seq peak, then blacklist-filter the result\n\n## Objective\n\nFor the CTCF ChIP-seq peak set from HFF cells (ENCODE, assembly GRCh38), assign to every peak the strongest CTCF motif from the JASPAR MA0139.1 track that overlaps it, and then conservatively remove any peak material lying within \u00b11 kb of ENCODE blacklisted genomic regions. The deliverable is a table of the retained peak intervals, each annotated with the peak's fold change and its assigned motif.\n\n## Supplied inputs (read-only; no network access)\n\n1. `/inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz` \u2014 CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF), gzipped narrowPeak, no header. Columns in order: `chrom, start, end, name, score, strand, fc, -log10p, -log10q, relSummit`. Only `chrom`, `start`, `end` and `fc` are used.\n2. `/inputs/MA0139.1.tsv.gz` \u2014 CTCF motif occurrences (JASPAR profile MA0139.1, hg38 UCSC track), gzipped, tab-separated. The file begins with a single UCSC track declaration line (not a data row); data rows follow with columns in order: `chrom, start, end, name, score, pval, strand`, where `pval` is the motif score expressed as \u2212log10(p-value) \u00d7 100.\n3. `/inputs/ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz` \u2014 ENCODE blacklist regions, gzipped BED3 (`chrom, start, end`), no header.\n\nAll coordinates are 0-based, half-open `[start, end)` intervals in base pairs on GRCh38/hg38. Chromosomes are matched by exact name string. Two intervals on the same chromosome overlap if they share at least one base (`start_A < end_B` and `start_B < end_A`); abutting intervals do not overlap.\n\n## Analysis specification\n\n1. **Motif assignment per peak.** Consider each distinct peak interval P = (chrom, start, end) in the peak set. Find all motif records whose interval overlaps P. The motif assigned to P is the overlapping motif with the largest `pval`; if several motifs tie for the largest `pval`, assign the one that appears earliest in the supplied motif track file's row order. A peak with no overlapping motif \u2014 or a peak none of whose overlapping motifs has a defined `pval` \u2014 is retained with blank motif fields.\n2. **Blacklist filtering, performed after assignment.** Expand every blacklist interval by 1000 bp on each side. Remove from each peak the portions covered by (sharing at least one base with) any expanded blacklist interval, keeping the surviving sub-intervals with start/end coordinates trimmed to the retained portion. A peak entirely covered by expanded blacklist intervals contributes no rows. Motif assignment is performed on the original, untrimmed peak spans; the blacklist step only trims the reported peak coordinates.\n\n## Required output\n\nWrite a single file `/outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv`: UTF-8, comma-separated, exactly one header line followed by one data row per retained peak sub-interval, no index column, no additional files. Columns, in exactly this order and with exactly these names:\n\n```\nchrom,start,end,fc,motif_chrom,motif_start,motif_end,motif_pval,motif_strand\n```\n\n- `chrom`, `start`, `end` \u2014 the retained (possibly trimmed) peak sub-interval; integers.\n- `fc` \u2014 the peak's fold-change value from the peaks file.\n- `motif_chrom`, `motif_start`, `motif_end` \u2014 the assigned motif's interval.\n- `motif_pval` \u2014 the assigned motif's `pval` score (\u2212log10 p \u00d7 100).\n- `motif_strand` \u2014 the assigned motif's strand (`+` or `-`).\n- Motif fields are blank for peaks with no assigned motif.\n- A peak split into several retained pieces appears once per piece, each row carrying the same `fc` and motif annotation.\n\nRow order is free and will not be evaluated. The analysis is fully deterministic; no randomness is involved.\n\n## Environment and resources\n\nRun offline. Limits: 4 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 600 s wall-clock. Any toolchain is acceptable provided the output meets the specification above; for convenience a Python environment including bioframe 0.8.0 is available, but its use is not required."
  }
}

Only one of pad\\n    or scale can be provided. Often followed by :func:`trim()`.\\n\\n    Parameters\\n    ----------\\n    df : pandas.DataFrame\\n\\n    pad : int, optional\\n        The amount by which the intervals are additively expanded *on each side*.\\n        Negative values for pad shrink intervals, but not beyond the interval\\n        midpoint. Either `pad` or `scale` must be supplied.\\n\\n    scale : float, optional\\n        The factor by which to scale intervals multiplicatively on each side, e.g\\n        ``scale=2`` doubles each interval, ``scale=0`` returns midpoints, and\\n        ``scale=1`` returns original intervals.       "instruction.md": "# Task: assign the strongest CTCF motif to each CTCF ChIP-seq peak, then blacklist-filter the result\n\n## Objective\n\nFor the CTCF ChIP-seq peak set from HFF cells (ENCODE, assembly GRCh38), assign to every peak the strongest CTCF motif from the JASPAR MA0139.1 track that overlaps it, and then conservatively remove any peak material lying within \u00b11 kb of ENCODE blacklisted genomic regions. The deliverable is a table of the retained peak intervals, each annotated with the peak's fold change and its assigned motif.\n\n## Supplied inputs (read-only; no network access)\n\n1. `/inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz` \u2014 CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF), gzipped narrowPeak, no header. Columns in order: `chrom, start, end, name, score, strand, fc, -log10p, -log10q, relSummit`. Only `chrom`, `start`, `end` and `fc` are used.\n2. `/inputs/MA0139.1.tsv.gz` \u2014 CTCF motif occurrences (JASPAR profile MA0139.1, hg38 UCSC track), gzipped, tab-separated. The file begins with a single UCSC track declaration line (not a data row); data rows follow with columns in order: `chrom, start, end, name, score, pval, strand`, where `pval` is the motif score expressed as \u2212log10(p-value) \u00d7 100.\n3. `/inputs/ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz` \u2014 ENCODE blacklist regions, gzipped BED3 (`chrom, start, end`), no header.\n\nAll coordinates are 0-based, half-open `[start, end)` intervals in base pairs on GRCh38/hg38. Chromosomes are matched by exact name string. Two intervals on the same chromosome overlap if they share at least one base (`start_A < end_B` and `start_B < end_A`); abutting intervals do not overlap.\n\n## Analysis specification\n\n1. **Motif assignment per peak.** Consider each distinct peak interval P = (chrom, start, end) in the peak set. Find all motif records whose interval overlaps P. The motif assigned to P is the overlapping motif with the largest `pval`; if several motifs tie for the largest `pval`, assign the one that appears earliest in the supplied motif track file's row order. A peak with no overlapping motif \u2014 or a peak none of whose overlapping motifs has a defined `pval` \u2014 is retained with blank motif fields.\n2. **Blacklist filtering, performed after assignment.** Expand every blacklist interval by 1000 bp on each side. Remove from each peak the portions covered by (sharing at least one base with) any expanded blacklist interval, keeping the surviving sub-intervals with start/end coordinates trimmed to the retained portion. A peak entirely covered by expanded blacklist intervals contributes no rows. Motif assignment is performed on the original, untrimmed peak spans; the blacklist step only trims the reported peak coordinates.\n\n## Input parsing and value conventions\n\n- The narrowPeak `fc` column (7th column) is a decimal number.\n- The motif track's first physical line is a UCSC track declaration (for example `track name=... `); skip it before reading data rows. Every data row has exactly the 7 tab-separated fields listed above.\n- Any blank line in a gzip input file is ignored.\n\n## Required output\n\nWrite a single file `outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv`: UTF-8, comma-separated, exactly one header line followed by one data row per retained peak sub-interval, no index column, no additional files. Columns, in exactly this order and with exactly these names:\n\n```\nchrom,start,end,fc,motif_chrom,motif_start,motif_end,motif_pval,motif_strand\n```\n\n- `chrom`, `start`, `end` \u2014 the retained (possibly trimmed) peak sub-interval; integers.\n- `fc` \u2014 the peak's fold-change value from the peaks file.\n- `motif_chrom`, `motif_start`, `motif_end` \u2014 the assigned motif's interval.\n- `motif_pval` \u2014 the assigned motif's `pval` score (\u2212log10 p \u00d7 100).\n- `motif_strand` \u2014 the assigned motif's strand (`+` or `-`).\n- Motif fields are blank for peaks with no assigned motif.\n- A peak split into several retained pieces appears once per piece, each row carrying the same `fc` and motif annotation.\n\nRow order is free and will not be evaluated. The analysis is fully deterministic; no randomness is involved.\n\n## Environment and resources\n\nRun offline. Limits: 4 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 600 s wall-clock. Any toolchain is acceptable provided the output meets the specification above; for convenience a Python environment including bioframe 0.8.0 is available, but its use is not required.\n\n",
      "oracle.py": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"solve.py -- assign the strongest CTCF motif to every CTCF ChIP-seq peak,\nthen conservatively trim the peaks around ENCODE blacklisted regions.\n\nClean-room implementation of the public task: plain gzip text parsing and\nexplicit interval arithmetic (no bioframe, no pandas). It reads only the\nfiles supplied in --input-dir and writes only into --output-dir.\n\nInputs (coordinates are 0-based half-open, GRCh38/hg38):\n  ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz  CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF), gzipped narrowPeak, no header\n  MA0139.1.tsv.gz     JASPAR MA0139.1 motif track, gzipped TSV; its first\n                      physical line is a UCSC track declaration (skipped)\n  ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz  ENCODE blacklist regions, gzipped BED3\nOutput:\n  ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv\n\"\"\"\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nimport gzip\nimport heapq\nimport os\n\nPEAK_FILE = \"ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz\"\nMOTIF_FILE = \"MA0139.1.tsv.gz\"\nBLACKLIST_FILE = \"ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz\"\nOUT_FILE = \"ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv\"\nPAD = 1000\nMOTIF_NCOLS = 7\n\n\ndef read_lines(path):\n    \"\"\"Yield the non-empty lines of a gzipped text file.\"\"\"\n    with gzip.open(path, \"rt\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n        for raw in fh:\n            line = raw.rstrip(\"\\n\").rstrip(\"\\r\")\n            if line.strip():\n                yield line\n\n\ndef load_peaks(path):\n    \"\"\"Return (chrom, start, end, fc) peak records in file order.\"\"\"\n    peaks = []\n    for line in read_lines(path):\n        f = line.split(\"\\t\")\n        if len(f) < 7:\n            raise ValueError(\"peak row with fewer than 7 columns: %r\" % line)\n        peaks.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2]), float(f[6])))\n    return peaks\n\n\ndef parse_pval(text):\n    \"\"\"Parse a motif pval; empty/NA fields are undefined (None).\"\"\"\n    text = text.strip()\n    if text in (\"\", \".\", \"NA\", \"nan\", \"NaN\", \"None\"):\n        return None\n    return float(text)\n\n\ndef load_motifs(path):\n    \"\"\"Return (chrom, start, end, pval, strand) motif records in row order.\n\n    pval is the motif score as -log10(p-value) * 100; it is None when the\n    supplied field does not define a score.\n    \"\"\"\n    motifs = []\n    seen_first_line = False\n    for line in read_lines(path):\n        f = line.split(\"\\t\")\n        if not seen_first_line:\n            seen_first_line = True\n            if len(f) != MOTIF_NCOLS:\n                continue  # UCSC track declaration, not a data row\n        if len(f) != MOTIF_NCOLS:\n            raise ValueError(\"motif row without exactly 7 columns: %r\" % line)\n        motifs.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2]), parse_pval(f[5]), f[6]))\n    return motifs\n\n\ndef load_blacklist(path):\n    \"\"\"Return (chrom, start, end) blacklist regions.\"\"\"\n    regions = []\n    for line in read_lines(path):\n        f = line.split(\"\\t\")\n        if len(f) < 3:\n            raise ValueError(\"blacklist row with fewer than 3 columns: %r\" % line)\n        regions.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2])))\n    return regions\n\n\ndef assign_motifs(peaks, motifs):\n    \"\"\"Return {peak interval: assigned motif record} for the peaks that have\n    at least one overlapping motif.\n\n    The assigned motif is the overlapping motif with the largest pval; if\n    several motifs tie for the largest pval, the earliest one in the motif\n    track's row order wins.  Peaks are collapsed to their distinct intervals.\n    \"\"\"\n    peaks_by_chrom = {}\n    for chrom, start, end, _fc in peaks:\n        peaks_by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, set()).add((start, end))\n\n    motifs_by_chrom = {}\n    for j, (chrom, start, end, pval, strand) in enumerate(motifs):\n        motifs_by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, []).append((start, end, pval, strand, j))\n\n    best = {}  # peak interval -> (-pval, motif row order), minimal wins\n    for chrom, pset in peaks_by_chrom.items():\n        mlist = motifs_by_chrom.get(chrom)\n        if not mlist:\n            continue\n        groups = sorted(pset)\n        msorted = sorted(mlist, key=lambda m: (m[0], m[4]))\n        mcursor = 0\n        active = []  # min-heap keyed by motif end\n        for gstart, gend in groups:\n            # admit every motif that starts before this peak ends\n            while mcursor < len(msorted) and msorted[mcursor][0] < gend:\n                ms, me, mp, mst, mj = msorted[mcursor]\n                heapq.heappush(active, (me, ms, mp, mst, mj))\n                mcursor += 1\n            # evict motifs that end at or before this peak starts\n            while active and active[0][0] <= gstart:\n                heapq.heappop(active)\n            # every remaining active motif shares at least one base with the peak\n            for _me, _ms, mp, _mst, mj in active:\n                if mp is None:\n                    continue  # undefined pval -> cannot be the strongest motif\n                cand = (-mp, mj)\n                cur = best.get((chrom, gstart, gend))\n                if cur is None or cand < cur:\n                    best[(chrom, gstart, gend)] = cand\n    return {k: motifs[v[1]] for k, v in best.items()}\n\n\ndef merged_expanded_blacklist(regions, pad):\n    \"\"\"Expand each blacklist interval by pad on both sides and merge per chrom.\n\n    Returns {chrom: sorted disjoint half-open intervals}.\n    \"\"\"\n    by_chrom = {}\n    for chrom, start, end in regions:\n        by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, []).append((start - pad, end + pad))\n    merged = {}\n    for chrom, ivs in by_chrom.items():\n        out = []\n        for s, e in sorted(ivs):\n            if out and s <= out[-1][1]:\n                if e > out[-1][1]:\n                    out[-1][1] = e\n            else:\n                out.append([s, e])\n        merged[chrom] = [tuple(iv) for iv in out]\n    return merged\n\n\ndef trim(start, end, cuts):\n    \"\"\"Subtract the sorted disjoint `cuts` intervals from [start, end).\"\"\"\n    pieces = []\n    cur = start\n    for cs, ce in cuts:\n        if ce <= cur:\n            continue\n        if cs <= cur:\n            cur = ce\n            continue\n        if cs >= end:\n            break\n        pieces.append((cur, cs))\n        cur = ce\n    if cur < end:\n        pieces.append((cur, end))\n    return [(s, e) for s, e in pieces if s < e]\n\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=\"Assign the strongest CTCF motif to each peak, then trim \"\n                    \"peaks within +/-1kb of ENCODE blacklist regions.\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--input-dir\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", required=True)\n    a = ap.parse_args()\n\n    peaks = load_peaks(os.path.join(a.input_dir, PEAK_FILE))\n    motifs = load_motifs(os.path.join(a.input_dir, MOTIF_FILE))\n    blacklist = load_blacklist(os.path.join(a.input_dir, BLACKLIST_FILE))\n    cuts = merged_expanded_blacklist(blacklist, PAD)\n    assigned = assign_motifs(peaks, motifs)\n\n    # distinct peak intervals in file order; a repeated interval is annotated\n    # with the fold change of its first record\n    groups = []\n    seen = set()\n    for chrom, start, end, fc in peaks:\n        key = (chrom, start, end)\n        if key in seen:\n            continue\n        seen.add(key)\n        groups.append(key + (fc,))\n\n    os.makedirs(a.output_dir, exist_ok=True)\n    out_path = os.path.join(a.output_dir, OUT_FILE)\n    with open(out_path, \"w\", newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        w = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n        w.writerow([\"chrom\", \"start\", \"end\", \"fc\",\n                    \"motif_chrom\", \"motif_start\", \"motif_end\",\n                    \"motif_pval\", \"motif_strand\"])\n        for chrom, start, end, fc in groups:\n            motif = assigned.get((chrom, start, end))\n            for s, e in trim(start, end, cuts.get(chrom, [])):\n                if motif is None:\n                    # no assigned motif: blank motif fields\n                    w.writerow([chrom, s, e, fc, \"\", \"\", \"\", \"\", \"\"])\n                else:\n                    w.writerow([chrom, s, e, fc,\n                                motif[0], motif[1], motif[2],\n                                float(motif[3]), motif[4]])\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n\n",
      "rationale.md": "Task scope: the notebook's single terminal artifact (df_peaks_maxmotif_clean) is re-described as a scientific question \u2014 per-peak strongest overlapping JASPAR MA0139.1 motif with CTCF ChIP-seq fold change, then conservative \u00b11 kb blacklist trimming of peak spans. All three original inputs are required and no intermediates need to be supplied (the analysis is a two-step interval problem from raw tracks), so the solver works directly from the original byte-exact files.\n\nProvenance of inputs: derive.py copies ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz (peaks), MA0139.1.tsv.gz (motifs) and ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz (blacklist) byte-for-byte from the recorded original input paths, verifying each sha256 against the source manifest (/work/original-inputs.json). Only destination/inputs/ and destination/reference/ are created. No supplied metadata had to be derived or reshaped, so cell/entity alignment is trivially the original file alignment (exact chromosome name strings, 0-based half-open intervals).\n\nReference projection: /work/reference/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv (40557 data rows) is copied line-by-line and only its header is rewritten to the public schema chrom,start,end,fc,motif_chrom,motif_start,motif_end,motif_pval,motif_strand (chrom_2/start_2/end_2/pval_2/strand_2 renamed). All values and all rows are passed through unchanged; derive.py hard-fails if the header is not the expected original header. Projected reference is supplied for grading only, not to the solver.\n\nValidation I actually ran in this stage:\n1. Independently re-executed the notebook's terminal variable (bioframe overlap \u2192 groupby idxmax on pval_2 with -1 fill \u2192 column select/rename \u2192 bioframe.subtract(df, bioframe.expand(blacklist,1000)) \u2192 to_csv) under the pinned venv: its output is byte-identical (sha256 8ba2ca5c...) to /work/reference/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv, so the recorded reference is faithful to the approved scope with this exact environment (bioframe 0.8.0, pandas 2.3.3).\n2. Wrote a clean-room oracle (pure stdlib: gzip parsing + sorted sweep/heap, no bioframe, no pandas, no reference access) matching the public text. Against the projected reference it produces 40557/40557 identical rows (exact string equality after header renaming, i.e. every value including fc/pval decimal forms matches).\n3. Edge cases checked with synthetic inputs: pval ties resolved by earliest motif row order, abutting motifs excluded, peak splitting into two retained pieces, peak fully removed by expanded blacklist, merged overlapping expanded blacklist intervals, per-chromosome isolation, and duplicated peak intervals (see leakage notes).\n4. Timing/resources: oracle runs in ~2 s wall and ~300 MB RSS, far inside the 600 s / 8 GiB limits. Full end-to-end (derive \u2192 oracle from a fresh directory with only inputs/) reproduces the projected reference exactly.\n\nDeliberate design decisions the grader should be aware of:\n- Peak grouping. The peaks file contains 15 repeated (chrom, start, end) intervals with different fc values. Collapsing peaks to distinct intervals (the notebook's implicit groupby semantics) yields exactly one row per distinct interval \u2014 40572 distinct intervals, of which 40557 survive trimming, matching the reference row count exactly with no leftover rows. The public spec therefore says \"each distinct peak interval P\". Any implementation that instead emits one row per peak record would produce 15 extra rows in untrimmed regions, which the comparison stage should reject as a deviation from the public text.\n- fc and motif_pval decimal formatting. The exported reference is a pandas float CSV, so fc and motif_pval are emitted with Python float repr (\"97.8\" not \"97.80\"; \"450.0\" not \"450\"). The oracle copies this convention verbatim (fc from float(field), pval as float()). The controller's comparison rules must compare these fields numerically (or normalize representations), otherwise legitimate scientific answers formatted differently would fail; this is the main remaining validation question for the comparison stage. Row order is already declared free by the approved spec and is genuinely free (the oracle's natural order happens to match, but that should not be graded).\n- Row order. Oracle writes peak groups in input-file order (same order as the reference), but the spec explicitly frees row order, so comparison should be order-insensitive on the tuple (chrom, start, end) identity or a row multiset.\n- Trimming versus assignment decoupling. Assignment uses the original untrimmed peak span; 1 surviving row (chr17:65556443-65556707, trimmed to 65556624-65556707) carries a motif that no longer overlaps the trimmed span. This is documented in the public text (\"Motif assignment is performed on the original, untrimmed peak spans\"); the comparison stage should not require the assigned motif to overlap the reported sub-interval.\n\nLeakage considerations: the reference table itself is the answer, so it must never reach the solver; the oracle only reads the three supplied inputs via --input-dir. No hidden caches, no reference answer values embedded, no incidental package naming conventions required (chromosome names are matched as exact strings; no assembly metadata or chrom-size tables are needed because subtraction is implemented per chromosome without a genome view). Off-target contigs in the motif track (e.g. chr11_KI270721v1_random) and odd peak contigs (chrM, chrUn_*, alt/random contigs) are all handled by the same exact-name grouping and are naturally unmatched/blank where appropriate, matching the reference.\n\nPending for later stages (not blocking): numeric rather than string comparison of fc/motif_pval, order-insensitive row comparison, and mutation-style tests (e.g. using the smaller copy of a peak record, tie-breaking by row order, abutting versus overlapping, \u00b11 kb pad on both sides only, trimming versus dropping whole peaks) which belong to the comparison worker. Disposition: ready.\n"

    "inputs/exports.py": "# --- Endpoint export: terminal scientific results ---\n\nimport os\n\nos.makedirs(\"/work/outputs\", exist_ok=True)\n\n# Final result of the tutorial: CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF, ENCODE ENCFF401MQL)\n# each assigned the strongest overlapping JASPAR CTCF motif (MA0139.1), with\n# peaks within +/-1kb of ENCODE blacklist regions (ENCFF356LFX) removed.\n# Written as-is from the dataframe produced by bioframe.subtract above.\ndf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.to_csv(\n    \"/work/outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv\", index=False\n)",
    "inputs/original.py": "# ---\n# jupyter:\n#   jupytext:\n#     text_representation:\n#       extension: .py\n#       format_name: nomarker\n#       format_version: '1.0'\n#       jupytext_version: 1.19.6\n#   kernelspec:\n#     display_name: Python 3.10\n#     language: python\n#     name: python3\n# ---\n\n# # How to: assign TF Motifs to ChIP-seq peaks\n#\n# This tutorial demonstrates one way to assign CTCF motifs to CTCF ChIP-seq peaks using bioframe.\n#\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nimport bioframe\n\nbase_dir = \"/tmp/bioframe_tutorial_data/\"\nassembly = \"GRCh38\"\n\n# ## Load CTCF ChIP-seq peaks for HFF from ENCODE\n#\n# This approach makes use of the `narrowPeak` schema for bioframe.read_table . \n\nctcf_peaks = bioframe.read_table(\n    \"https://www.encodeproject.org/files/ENCFF401MQL/@@download/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz\",\n    schema=\"narrowPeak\",\n)\nctcf_peaks[0:5]\n\n# ## Get CTCF motifs from JASPAR\n\n### CTCF motif: http://jaspar.genereg.net/matrix/MA0139.1/\njaspar_url = \"http://expdata.cmmt.ubc.ca/JASPAR/downloads/UCSC_tracks/2022/hg38/\"\njaspar_motif_file = \"MA0139.1.tsv.gz\"\nctcf_motifs = bioframe.read_table(\n    jaspar_url + jaspar_motif_file, schema=\"jaspar\", skiprows=1\n)\nctcf_motifs[0:4]\n\n# ## Overlap peaks & motifs\n\ndf_peaks_motifs = bioframe.overlap(\n    ctcf_peaks, ctcf_motifs, suffixes=(\"_1\", \"_2\"), return_index=True\n)\n\n# There are often multiple motifs overlapping one ChIP-seq peak, and a substantial number of peaks without motifs:\n\n# note that counting motifs per peak can also be handled directly with\n# bioframe.count_overlaps but since we re-use df_peaks_motifs below we\n# instead use the pandas operations directly\nmotifs_per_peak = df_peaks_motifs.groupby([\"index_1\"])[\"index_2\"].count().values\n\nplt.hist(motifs_per_peak, np.arange(0, np.max(motifs_per_peak)))\nplt.xlabel(\"number of overlapping motifs per peak\")\nplt.ylabel(\"number of peaks\")\nplt.semilogy()\n\nprint(\n    f\"fraction of peaks without motifs \"\n    f\"{np.round(np.sum(motifs_per_peak == 0) / len(motifs_per_peak), 2)}\"\n)\n\n# ### Assign the strongest motif to each peak\n\n# since idxmax does not currently take NA, fill with -1\ndf_peaks_motifs[\"pval_2\"] = Constructed scientific question

transfer/bioframe/materialization-runs/005/instruction.md

Task: assign the strongest CTCF motif to each CTCF ChIP-seq peak, then blacklist-filter the result

Objective

For the CTCF ChIP-seq peak set from HFF cells (ENCODE, assembly GRCh38), assign to every peak the strongest CTCF motif from the JASPAR MA0139.1 track that overlaps it, and then conservatively remove any peak material lying within ±1 kb of ENCODE blacklisted genomic regions. The deliverable is a table of the retained peak intervals, each annotated with the peak's fold change and its assigned motif.

Supplied inputs (read-only; no network access)

  1. /inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz — CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF), gzipped narrowPeak, no header. 40587 rows, each with 10 tab-separated fields in order: chrom, start, end, name, score, strand, fc, -log10p, -log10q, relSummit. Only chrom, start, end and fc are used; fc (the 7th field) is a decimal number.
  2. /inputs/MA0139.1.tsv.gz — CTCF motif occurrences (JASPAR profile MA0139.1, hg38 UCSC track), gzipped, tab-separated. Data rows have exactly 7 tab-separated fields in order: chrom, start, end, name, score, pval, strand, where pval is the motif score expressed as −log10(p-value) × 100 (an integer value in this file). The file contains 770050 data rows and no header or track-declaration lines; every decompressed line in the supplied file conforms to this schema. A line that does not conform to the 7-field data-row schema (for example a UCSC track declaration, should one be present) is not a data record and must be ignored, as must any blank line.
  3. /inputs/ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz — ENCODE blacklist regions, gzipped BED3 (chrom, start, end), no header, 910 rows.

All coordinates are 0-based, half-open [start, end) intervals in base pairs on GRCh38/hg38. Chromosomes are matched by exact name string (no aliasing or prefix normalization). Two intervals on the same chromosome overlap if they share at least one base (start_A < end_B and start_B < end_A); abutting intervals do not overlap.

Entities, output grain and combination rules

  • The output entities are distinct peak intervals, not peak records. The peaks file contains 40587 records over 40572 distinct (chrom, start, end) intervals; 15 intervals appear in two records each, with different fc values. Each distinct interval is analyzed and reported as one peak, annotated with the fc of the first record of that interval in the peaks file's row order (the file is sorted ascending by fc, so this is also the smaller of the two values).
  • A peak interval can be overlapped by zero, one or many motif records (many is common); the assignment rule below selects a single motif or none.
  • Peaks are neither merged nor re-clustered; each distinct interval is handled independently.

Analysis specification

  1. Motif assignment per peak. For each distinct peak interval P = (chrom, start, end), find all motif records whose interval overlaps P. The motif assigned to P is the overlapping motif with the largest pval; if several motifs tie for the largest pval (such ties do occur for some peaks in this dataset), assign the one that appears earliest in the motif track file's row order. A peak with no overlapping motif — or a peak none of whose overlapping motifs has a defined pval — is retained with blank motif fields. (Every pval in the supplied motif file is defined.)
  2. Blacklist filtering, performed after assignment. Expand every blacklist interval by 1000 bp on each side and take the union of the expanded intervals (equivalently: first merge expanded intervals that overlap or abut one another). Remove from each peak the portions covered by (sharing at least one base with) the removed set, keeping the surviving sub-intervals with start/end coordinates trimmed to the retained portion. A peak entirely covered by expanded blacklist intervals contributes no rows. Motif assignment is performed on the original, untrimmed peak spans; the blacklist step only trims the reported peak coordinates, so a retained row's assigned motif need not overlap the trimmed sub-interval it is reported on.

Required output

Write a single file /outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv: UTF-8, comma-separated, exactly one header line followed by one data row per retained peak sub-interval, no index column, no additional files. Columns, in exactly this order and with exactly these names:

chrom,start,end,fc,motif_chrom,motif_start,motif_end,motif_pval,motif_strand
  • chrom, start, end — the retained (possibly trimmed) peak sub-interval; integers.
  • fc — the peak's fold-change value, per the entity rule above.
  • motif_chrom, motif_start, motif_end — the assigned motif's interval; motif_start and motif_end are integers.
  • motif_pval — the assigned motif's pval score (−log10 p × 100).
  • motif_strand — the assigned motif's strand (+ or -).
  • Motif fields are blank for peaks with no assigned motif.
  • A peak split into several retained pieces appears once per piece, each row carrying the same fc and motif annotation.

Row order is free and will not be evaluated. fc and motif_pval are decimal numbers; any unambiguous decimal representation of the value is acceptable (for example 450 or 450.0). The analysis is fully deterministic; no randomness is involved.

Environment and resources

Run offline. Limits: 4 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 600 s wall-clock. Any toolchain is acceptable provided the output meets the specification above; for convenience a Python environment including bioframe 0.8.0 is available, but its use is not required.

Input/reference derivation

transfer/bioframe/materialization-runs/005/derive.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage the read-only solver inputs and project the reference answer table.

This performs no scientific computation:
  * the three original input files (ENCODE CTCF peaks for HFF, JASPAR MA0139.1
    motif track, ENCODE blacklist) are copied byte-for-byte into
    <destination>/inputs/,
  * the terminal reference export is copied into <destination>/reference/
    with only its motif columns renamed to the public output schema
    (chrom_2 -> motif_chrom, start_2 -> motif_start, end_2 -> motif_end,
    pval_2 -> motif_pval, strand_2 -> motif_strand); every value and every
    row is passed through unchanged.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil

INPUT_BASENAMES = (
    "ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz",
    "MA0139.1.tsv.gz",
    "ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz",
)
REF_FILE = "ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv"

ORIGINAL_HEADER = [
    "chrom", "start", "end", "fc",
    "chrom_2", "start_2", "end_2", "pval_2", "strand_2",
]
PUBLIC_HEADER = [
    "chrom", "start", "end", "fc",
    "motif_chrom", "motif_start", "motif_end", "motif_pval", "motif_strand",
]


def sha256(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def stage_inputs(manifest_path, inputs_dir):
    with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        manifest = json.load(fh)
    entries = {os.path.basename(e["local_path"]): e for e in manifest.get("files", [])}
    copied = []
    for name in INPUT_BASENAMES:
        entry = entries.get(name)
        if entry is None:
            raise SystemExit(f"input {name} missing from source manifest")
        src = entry["local_path"]
        if not os.path.exists(src):
            raise SystemExit(f"input {name} not found at {src}")
        digest = sha256(src)
        if digest != entry["sha256"]:
            raise SystemExit(f"input {name} hash mismatch: {digest} != {entry['sha256']}")
        dst = os.path.join(inputs_dir, name)
        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)
        if sha256(dst) != digest:
            raise SystemExit(f"copy of {name} is not byte-identical")
        copied.append((name, digest))
    return copied


def project_reference(reference_dir, reference_out):
    src = os.path.join(reference_dir, REF_FILE)
    if not os.path.exists(src):
        raise SystemExit(f"reference export not found at {src}")
    lines_read = 0
    with open(src, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fin, \
            open(reference_out, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fout:
        for lineno, line in enumerate(fin):
            if lineno == 0:
                fields = line.rstrip("\r\n").split(",")
                if fields != ORIGINAL_HEADER:
                    raise SystemExit(f"unexpected reference header: {fields!r}")
                fout.write(",".join(PUBLIC_HEADER) + "\n")
            else:
                fout.write(line)
            lines_read += 1
    if lines_read < 2:
        raise SystemExit("reference export has no data rows")
    return lines_read - 1


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--source-inputs", required=True,
                    help="JSON manifest of the original input files")
    ap.add_argument("--reference-dir", required=True,
                    help="directory holding the original terminal artifacts")
    ap.add_argument("--destination", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    inputs_dir = os.path.join(args.destination, "inputs")
    reference_dir = os.path.join(args.destination, "reference")
    os.makedirs(inputs_dir, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(reference_dir, exist_ok=True)

    staged = stage_inputs(args.source_inputs, inputs_dir)
    rows = project_reference(args.reference_dir,
                             os.path.join(reference_dir, REF_FILE))
    for name, digest in staged:
        print(f"staged inputs/{name} sha256={digest}")
    print(f"projected reference/{REF_FILE}: {rows} data rows, columns renamed "
          f"to the public schema")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""solve.py -- assign the strongest CTCF motif to every CTCF ChIP-seq peak,
then conservatively trim the peaks around ENCODE blacklisted regions.

Clean-room implementation of the public task: plain gzip text parsing and
explicit interval arithmetic (no bioframe, no pandas). It reads only the
files supplied in --input-dir and writes only into --output-dir.

Inputs (coordinates are 0-based half-open, GRCh38/hg38):
  ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz  CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF), gzipped narrowPeak, no header
  MA0139.1.tsv.gz     JASPAR MA0139.1 motif track, gzipped TSV; each data row
                      has exactly 7 tab-separated fields, and a leading line
                      that is not a 7-field data row (e.g. a UCSC track
                      declaration) is skipped if one is present
  ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz  ENCODE blacklist regions, gzipped BED3
Output:
  ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv
"""
import argparse
import csv
import gzip
import heapq
import os

PEAK_FILE = "ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz"
MOTIF_FILE = "MA0139.1.tsv.gz"
BLACKLIST_FILE = "ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz"
OUT_FILE = "ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv"
PAD = 1000
MOTIF_NCOLS = 7


def read_lines(path):
    """Yield the non-empty lines of a gzipped text file."""
    with gzip.open(path, "rt", newline="") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.rstrip("\n").rstrip("\r")
            if line.strip():
                yield line


def load_peaks(path):
    """Return (chrom, start, end, fc) peak records in file order."""
    peaks = []
    for line in read_lines(path):
        f = line.split("\t")
        if len(f) < 7:
            raise ValueError("peak row with fewer than 7 columns: %r" % line)
        peaks.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2]), float(f[6])))
    return peaks


def parse_pval(text):
    """Parse a motif pval; empty/NA fields are undefined (None)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if text in ("", ".", "NA", "nan", "NaN", "None"):
        return None
    return float(text)


def load_motifs(path):
    """Return (chrom, start, end, pval, strand) motif records in row order.

    pval is the motif score as -log10(p-value) * 100; it is None when the
    supplied field does not define a score.
    """
    motifs = []
    seen_first_line = False
    for line in read_lines(path):
        f = line.split("\t")
        if not seen_first_line:
            seen_first_line = True
            if len(f) != MOTIF_NCOLS:
                continue  # UCSC track declaration, not a data row
        if len(f) != MOTIF_NCOLS:
            raise ValueError("motif row without exactly 7 columns: %r" % line)
        motifs.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2]), parse_pval(f[5]), f[6]))
    return motifs


def load_blacklist(path):
    """Return (chrom, start, end) blacklist regions."""
    regions = []
    for line in read_lines(path):
        f = line.split("\t")
        if len(f) < 3:
            raise ValueError("blacklist row with fewer than 3 columns: %r" % line)
        regions.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2])))
    return regions


def assign_motifs(peaks, motifs):
    """Return {peak interval: assigned motif record} for the peaks that have
    at least one overlapping motif.

    The assigned motif is the overlapping motif with the largest pval; if
    several motifs tie for the largest pval, the earliest one in the motif
    track's row order wins.  Peaks are collapsed to their distinct intervals.
    """
    peaks_by_chrom = {}
    for chrom, start, end, _fc in peaks:
        peaks_by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, set()).add((start, end))

    motifs_by_chrom = {}
    for j, (chrom, start, end, pval, strand) in enumerate(motifs):
        motifs_by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, []).append((start, end, pval, strand, j))

    best = {}  # peak interval -> (-pval, motif row order), minimal wins
    for chrom, pset in peaks_by_chrom.items():
        mlist = motifs_by_chrom.get(chrom)
        if not mlist:
            continue
        groups = sorted(pset)
        msorted = sorted(mlist, key=lambda m: (m[0], m[4]))
        mcursor = 0
        active = []  # min-heap keyed by motif end
        for gstart, gend in groups:
            # admit every motif that starts before this peak ends
            while mcursor < len(msorted) and msorted[mcursor][0] < gend:
                ms, me, mp, mst, mj = msorted[mcursor]
                heapq.heappush(active, (me, ms, mp, mst, mj))
                mcursor += 1
            # evict motifs that end at or before this peak starts
            while active and active[0][0] <= gstart:
                heapq.heappop(active)
            # every remaining active motif shares at least one base with the peak
            for _me, _ms, mp, _mst, mj in active:
                if mp is None:
                    continue  # undefined pval -> cannot be the strongest motif
                cand = (-mp, mj)
                cur = best.get((chrom, gstart, gend))
                if cur is None or cand < cur:
                    best[(chrom, gstart, gend)] = cand
    return {k: motifs[v[1]] for k, v in best.items()}


def merged_expanded_blacklist(regions, pad):
    """Expand each blacklist interval by pad on both sides and merge per chrom.

    Returns {chrom: sorted disjoint half-open intervals}.
    """
    by_chrom = {}
    for chrom, start, end in regions:
        by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, []).append((start - pad, end + pad))
    merged = {}
    for chrom, ivs in by_chrom.items():
        out = []
        for s, e in sorted(ivs):
            if out and s <= out[-1][1]:
                if e > out[-1][1]:
                    out[-1][1] = e
            else:
                out.append([s, e])
        merged[chrom] = [tuple(iv) for iv in out]
    return merged


def trim(start, end, cuts):
    """Subtract the sorted disjoint `cuts` intervals from [start, end)."""
    pieces = []
    cur = start
    for cs, ce in cuts:
        if ce <= cur:
            continue
        if cs <= cur:
            cur = ce
            continue
        if cs >= end:
            break
        pieces.append((cur, cs))
        cur = ce
    if cur < end:
        pieces.append((cur, end))
    return [(s, e) for s, e in pieces if s < e]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Assign the strongest CTCF motif to each peak, then trim "
                    "peaks within +/-1kb of ENCODE blacklist regions.")
    ap.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    peaks = load_peaks(os.path.join(a.input_dir, PEAK_FILE))
    motifs = load_motifs(os.path.join(a.input_dir, MOTIF_FILE))
    blacklist = load_blacklist(os.path.join(a.input_dir, BLACKLIST_FILE))
    cuts = merged_expanded_blacklist(blacklist, PAD)
    assigned = assign_motifs(peaks, motifs)

    # distinct peak intervals in file order; a repeated interval is annotated
    # with the fold change of its first record
    groups = []
    seen = set()
    for chrom, start, end, fc in peaks:
        key = (chrom, start, end)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        groups.append(key + (fc,))

    os.makedirs(a.output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = os.path.join(a.output_dir, OUT_FILE)
    with open(out_path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(["chrom", "start", "end", "fc",
                    "motif_chrom", "motif_start", "motif_end",
                    "motif_pval", "motif_strand"])
        for chrom, start, end, fc in groups:
            motif = assigned.get((chrom, start, end))
            for s, e in trim(start, end, cuts.get(chrom, [])):
                if motif is None:
                    # no assigned motif: blank motif fields
                    w.writerow([chrom, s, e, fc, "", "", "", "", ""])
                else:
                    w.writerow([chrom, s, e, fc,
                                motif[0], motif[1], motif[2],
                                float(motif[3]), motif[4]])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

GLM-5.3 + deterministic controls

07 · Validate scientific comparison

Reexecute an answer-blind implementation, author the grader and probes, check mutation execution before freezing probes, and validate the final acceptance wording against executed controls. Recorded prompts and role inputs are shown separately.

Program: grading_session.py

Prompts

Independent implementation prompt

transfer/bioframe/grading-runs/002/independent/system-prompt.md

Independently implement the public scientific task for validation

You receive only the public question, supplied task inputs, required output paths, installed environment and execution limits. You do not receive the reference answers or its solution code. This is a validation implementation, not the final blind benchmark attempt. It cannot establish universal software portability.

Use the offline shell to inspect inputs and develop a standalone Python program accepting --input-dir PATH and --output-dir PATH. Write only in your working directory and supplied output directory. Private answer/author directories are inaccessible; do not try to bypass those boundaries. Follow the public scientific requirements. Prefer an independent implementation from basic numerical/statistical primitives where practical; do not simply assume a high-level method with a similar name has the requested options or definitions. Do not change the scientific method to obtain a convenient answer. Report ambiguity rather than guess hidden rules.

Submit disposition: ready, the complete code, and a concise private rationale explaining methods and any limitations. The controller runs your program on the supplied inputs from a fresh output directory and returns execution failures for repair. It does not expose expected values or numerical grading feedback in this session. A later stage compares your outputs, examines scientific differences and validates acceptance rules. Do not claim agreement you have not observed.

Keep the implementation and inspection focused; submit a complete program rather than building your own grader or mutation suite. If blocked, return disposition: blocked, an empty code string and a specific explanation.

Shell execution

Keep diagnostics concise: print aggregate checks and representative examples. Save complete listings to scratch files and inspect selected sections instead of streaming all rows, arrays or mismatches into the conversation.

Run commands in the foreground. Each shell call terminates its remaining child processes when it returns; background/nohup work cannot continue between calls. For longer computations, explicitly set timeout_sec up to the supplied reference_seconds limit (the shell default is 120 seconds). Save useful results to files before returning, then inspect them in later calls.

Grader author prompt

transfer/bioframe/grading-runs/002/grader/system-prompt.md

Construct a scientific-content grader for the specified task

You are the GLM grading worker. Produce a public acceptance contract and a deterministic Python grader for the already specified task. Preserve its scientific question and selected outputs. Earlier notebook exports may include branches now excluded by the approved task policy; do not reinstate them. This stage evaluates saved outputs and available recomputations; it does not construct a Harbor image.

Inputs and tools

The user message contains the current task question, source/export evidence, task policy, measured repeatability results and available execution records. Use those executed records for validation facts; earlier planning proposals are not additional requirements or evidence that a check has run. It names the directory containing private reference output files in your sandbox. The shell tool runs offline with the reference's resolved Python packages. You can inspect those output files and installed package sources, and experiment in your writable working directory. You cannot modify the controller's reference copies. When paths supplies task inputs and recomputed outputs, inspect those as recorded evidence too. Otherwise raw biological inputs are not available. Do not rerun the entire analysis in this grader-author stage; independently executed controls are the evidence for recomputation agreement.

Use submit_artifact (or revise_artifact after rejection) to return the complete candidate: public instructions, grader code, named checks and rationale. Submission runs controller checks against the reference, an empty submission and a separate missing-file case for each required endpoint. Rejections return actual evidence; repair the candidate, never the reference data or the target scientific methods. A separate worker will generate scientific counterexamples without seeing your grader. In a repair session, those frozen probes and measured failures are supplied.

Public contract

Return only the acceptance-rule addendum in instruction; the controller retains and combines it with the approved scientific question. Do not replace the question with a function-by-function reference recipe. Resolve representational ambiguities without changing the scientific target. If the target itself is contradictory, report a blocker. Keep software choice open and distinguish demonstrated agreement from untested portability. Never disclose measured answer values or private hashes.

Specify exactly what is compared: files, identifiers, columns, row alignment and ordering, duplicates, missing values, nonfinite numbers, categorical identities, and numeric comparisons. Every acceptance rule must appear in the public text. Explain cross-file consistency without confusing tables with different row units. Distinguish potentially missing annotations from mandatory identifiers/assignments.

Independently executed outputs are a comparison attempt, not a second oracle. Successful execution proves neither scientific correctness nor agreement with the public question. Diagnose disagreements against the stated task, source evidence and inspected data. Do not broaden acceptance or change entity identity merely to make that control pass. If the independent program or the public contract needs repair beyond this grader stage, return disposition: blocked with the specific reason. The controller cannot repair those scientific artifacts for you.

An equivalence rule must account for every accepted record and value. Retaining correct answers while appending unsupported values is not a valid alternative. Check coverage and multiplicity as well as membership; do not replace the requested output grain with a coarser set comparison to conceal a disagreement.

Use the measured repeatability evidence. Byte-identical reference runs do not make file hashes an appropriate grader or establish cross-stack portability. Compare parsed scientific content, retaining precision and identity. Establish any tolerance from a stated numerical/serialization argument and test its boundary; do not invent a generous threshold, round away meaningful errors, or copy a universal epsilon onto unrelated quantities. Exact comparison is permissible where justified and publicly stated. Reject nonfinite/invalid values explicitly; never let NaN make a numerical failure disappear. Preserve meaningful zero values. Normalize representation differences only when their consequences for every dependent endpoint are resolved and can be validated. Use stable identifiers for alignment; arbitrary row order is not a scientific target. Validate uniqueness, coverage and multiplicity before normalization. Do not require original row order or literal arbitrary labels merely because the reference used them. Do not add those equivalences just because they sound plausible. No independent software-equivalence claim can be established by modifying a copy of reference outputs. Use supplied independently executed outputs when establishing numerical rules. Do not mistake synthetic edits of answers for independent recomputation. If evidence is insufficient for a claimed tolerance or freedom, report the specific missing check rather than substituting an exact-recipe requirement.

Keep this stage focused: inspect the needed data properties, implement the comparator, and submit a complete candidate. Controller submission executes basic controls; a separate worker owns the independent mutation suite. Do not duplicate that suite or spend the session repeatedly auditing unrelated source internals.

Repair sessions

When a prior candidate and review are supplied, repair the identified defects in that candidate. Keep the supplied check definitions and frozen probes unchanged; report a blocker if a scientific change to either is necessary. Correct misleading explanations in the addendum or private rationale without changing the acceptance criteria. Describe numeric tolerances as limits on observable output differences, not as guarantees that every use of a particular wrong method will be detected. Keep run-specific calibration measurements and test history in the private rationale.

Use targeted tests for the changed behavior, then submit the complete candidate. The controller reruns all frozen controls on submission. Do not reconstruct their scripts, repeatedly run the entire suite locally, or expand into unrelated edge cases after the reported defects are resolved. Repeat a test only when a relevant code change, failed check, or unresolved review finding justifies it. Submission feedback is the next step; a local passing test is not final acceptance.

Grader interface

Return grader_code as a complete Python program. It accepts exactly:

python grade.py --reference-dir PATH --submission-dir PATH --report PATH

Reference and submission directories contain only the declared endpoint files. Read reference values dynamically; do not embed answer arrays, expected dimensions, cluster counts or result hashes. Never import or execute submission code. Treat missing, malformed, duplicate, out-of-range and nonfinite data as failed checks, not successful runs or uncaught exceptions. Do not use paths, timestamps, environment variables or probe names to identify which control is running. Do not write to reference or submission files. Network access is unavailable.

Write this JSON object to --report, with no additional keys:

{"passed": true, "checks": [{"id": "check_id", "passed": true, "message": "..."}]}

Emit every declared check exactly once even for empty or malformed submissions. passed is the conjunction of all check booleans. Exit 0 after writing a valid report for either a correct or incorrect submission. A crash or timeout is an incomplete verification, not evidence of rejecting a wrong scientific result. Use only the installed packages and finish within the supplied verifier deadline.

Declare each check's unique id, kind (structural or scientific), covered artifact paths, and public requirement. Split distinct scientific results into meaningful named checks so controls can target them; do not hide an independent branch behind a superficial schema or file-existence check. Every required artifact must have scientific coverage, including scientifically meaningful metadata. Cross-file checks may cover several artifacts. Do not add arbitrary numbers of checks or unrelated requirements.

The rationale is private: justify comparison choices, cite source/serialization facts, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and state unresolved limitations. An accepted candidate still requires independent probes, review and later Harbor packaging validation. It does not yet constitute a released task.

If blocked, submit disposition: "blocked" and explain the evidence gap in the private rationale/concerns. Ready artifacts use disposition: "ready". A blocked submission stops this stage; do not fabricate a candidate just to fill the schema.

Shell execution

Keep diagnostics concise: print aggregate checks and representative examples. Save complete listings to scratch files and inspect selected sections instead of streaming all rows, arrays or mismatches into the conversation.

Run commands in the foreground. Each shell call terminates its remaining child processes when it returns; background/nohup work cannot continue between calls. When a claimed equivalence permits multiple records or values for one entity, challenge it by retaining correct answers and adding a plausible but unsupported value, not only by inserting exact duplicates. Acceptance-text prompt

transfer/bioframe/grading-runs/004/contract/system-prompt.md

Correct explanations in an already executed acceptance contract

You receive a task, a grader candidate whose controls passed, and review feedback. Return corrected public acceptance text and a private rationale using the supplied schema. This is a prose-only stage: no shell or scientific execution is needed. The controller retains the exact grader code and check inventory, then reruns the controls and review. It reads only the\nfiles supplied in --input-dir and writes only into --output-dir.\n\nInputs (coordinates are 0-based half-open, GRCh38/hg38):\n  ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz  CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF), gzipped narrowPeak, no header\n  MA0139.1.tsv.gz     JASPAR MA0139.1 motif track, gzipped TSV; each data row\n                      has exactly 7 tab-separated fields, and a leading line\n                      that is not a 7-field data row (e.g. a UCSC track\n                      declaration) is skipped if one is present\n  ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz  ENCODE blacklist regions, gzipped BED3\nOutput:\n  ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv\n\"\"\"\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nimport gzip\nimport heapq\nimport os\n\nPEAK_FILE = \"ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz\"\nMOTIF_FILE = \"MA0139.1.tsv.gz\"\nBLACKLIST_FILE = \"ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz\"\nOUT_FILE = \"ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv\"\nPAD = 1000\nMOTIF_NCOLS = 7\n\n\ndef read_lines(path):\n    \"\"\"Yield the non-empty lines of a gzipped text file.\"\"\"\n    with gzip.open(path, \"rt\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n        for raw in fh:\n            line = raw.rstrip(\"\\n\").rstrip(\"\\r\")\n            if line.strip():\n                yield line\n\n\ndef load_peaks(path):\n    \"\"\"Return (chrom, start, end, fc) peak records in file order.\"\"\"\n    peaks = []\n    for line in read_lines(path):\n        f = line.split(\"\\t\")\n        if len(f) < 7:\n            raise ValueError(\"peak row with fewer than 7 columns: %r\" % line)\n        peaks.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2]), float(f[6])))\n    return peaks\n\n\ndef parse_pval(text):\n    \"\"\"Parse a motif pval; empty/NA fields are undefined (None).\"\"\"\n    text = text.strip()\n    if text in (\"\", \".\", \"NA\", \"nan\", \"NaN\", \"None\"):\n        return None\n    return float(text)\n\n\ndef load_motifs(path):\n    \"\"\"Return (chrom, start, end, pval, strand) motif records in row order.\n\n    pval is the motif score as -log10(p-value) * 100; it is None when the\n    supplied field does not define a score.\n    \"\"\"\n    motifs = []\n    seen_first_line = False\n    for line in read_lines(path):\n        f = line.split(\"\\t\")\n        if not seen_first_line:\n            seen_first_line = True\n            if len(f) != MOTIF_NCOLS:\n                continue  # UCSC track declaration, not a data row\n        if len(f) != MOTIF_NCOLS:\n            raise ValueError(\"motif row without exactly 7 columns: %r\" % line)\n        motifs.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2]), parse_pval(f[5]), f[6]))\n    return motifs\n\n\ndef load_blacklist(path):\n    \"\"\"Return (chrom, start, end) blacklist regions.\"\"\"\n    regions = []\n    for line in read_lines(path):\n        f = line.split(\"\\t\")\n        if len(f) < 3:\n            raise ValueError(\"blacklist row with fewer than 3 columns: %r\" % line)\n        regions.append((f[0], int(f[1]), int(f[2])))\n    return regions\n\n\ndef assign_motifs(peaks, motifs):\n    \"\"\"Return {peak interval: assigned motif record} for the peaks that have\n    at least one overlapping motif.\n\n    The assigned motif is the overlapping motif with the largest pval; if\n    several motifs tie for the largest pval, the earliest one in the motif\n    track's row order wins.  Peaks are collapsed to their distinct intervals.\n    \"\"\"\n    peaks_by_chrom = {}\n    for chrom, start, end, _fc in peaks:\n        peaks_by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, set()).add((start, end))\n\n interval -> (-pval, motif row order), minimal wins\n    for chrom, pset in peaks_by_chrom.items():\n        mlist = motifs_by_chrom.get(chrom)\n        if not mlist:\n            continue\n        groups = sorted(pset)\n        msorted = sorted(mlist, key=lambda m: (m[0], m[4]))\n        mcursor = 0\n        active = []  # min-heap keyed by motif end\n        for gstart, gend in groups:\n            # admit every motif that starts before this peak ends\n            while mcursor < len(msorted) and msorted[mcursor][0] < gend:\n                ms, me, mp, mst, mj = msorted[mcursor]\n gstart:\n                heapq.heappop(active)\n            # every remaining active motif shares at least one base with the peak\n            for _me, _ms, mp, _mst, mj in active:\n                if if cur is None or cand < cur:\n                    best[(chrom, gstart, gend)] = cand\n    return {k: motifs[v[1]] for k, v in best.items()}\n\n\ndef merged_expanded_blacklist(regions, pad):\n    \"\"\"Expand each blacklist interval by pad on both sides and merge per chrom.\n\n    Returns {chrom: sorted disjoint half-open intervals}.\n    \"\"\"\n    by_chrom = {}\n    for chrom, start, end in regions:\n        by_chrom.setdefault(chrom, []).append((start - pad, end + pad))\n    merged = {}\n    for chrom, ivs in by_chrom.items():\n        out = []\n        for s, e in sorted(ivs):\n iv in out]\n    return merged\n\n\ndef trim(start, end, cuts):\n    \"\"\"Subtract the sorted disjoint `cuts` intervals from [start, end).\"\"\"\n    pieces = []\n    cur = start\n    for cs, ce in cuts:\n        if ce <= cur:\n            continue\n        if cs <= cur:\n            cur = ce\n            continue\n        if cs >= end:\n            break\n        pieces.append((cur, cs))\n        cur = ce\n    if cur < end:\n        pieces.append((cur, end))\n    return [(s, e) for s, e in pieces if s < e]\n\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=\"Assign the strongest CTCF motif to each peak, then trim \"\n                    \"peaks within +/-1kb of ENCODE blacklist regions.\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--input-dir\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", required=True)\n    a = ap.parse_args()\n\n    peaks = load_peaks(os.path.join(a.input_dir, PEAK_FILE))\n    motifs = load_motifs(os.path.join(a.input_dir, \"start\", \"end\", \"fc\",\n                    \"motif_chrom\", \"motif_start\", \"motif_end\",\n                    \"motif_pval\", \"motif_strand\"])\n        for chrom, start, end, fc in groups:\n            motif = assigned.get((chrom, start, end))\n            for s, e in trim(start, end, cuts.get(chrom, [])):\n                if motif is None:\n                    # no assigned 1.19.6\n#   kernelspec:\n#     display_name: Python 3.10\n#     language: python\n#     name: python3\n# ---\n\n# # How to: assign TF Motifs to ChIP-seq peaks\n#\n# This tutorial demonstrates one way to assign CTCF motifs to CTCF ChIP-seq peaks using bioframe.\n#\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nimport bioframe\n\nbase_dir = \"/tmp/bioframe_tutorial_data/\"\nassembly = \"GRCh38\"\n\n# ## Load CTCF ChIP-seq peaks for HFF from ENCODE\n#\n# This approach makes use of the `narrowPeak` schema for bioframe.read_table . \n\nctcf_peaks = bioframe.read_table(\n    \"https://www.encodeproject.org/files/ENCFF401MQL/@@download/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz\",\n    schema=\"narrowPeak\",\n)\nctcf_peaks[0:5]\n\n# ## Get CTCF motifs from JASPAR\n\n### CTCF motif: http://jaspar.genereg.net/matrix/MA0139.1/\njaspar_url = \"http://expdata.cmmt.ubc.ca/JASPAR/downloads/UCSC_tracks/2022/hg38/\"\njaspar_motif_file = \"MA0139.1.tsv.gz\"\nctcf_motifs = bioframe.read_table(\n    jaspar_url + jaspar_motif_file, schema=\"jaspar\", skiprows=1\n)\nctcf_motifs[0:4]\n\n# ## Overlap peaks & motifs\n\ndf_peaks_motifs = bioframe.overlap(\n    ctcf_peaks, ctcf_motifs, suffixes=(\"_1\", \"_2\"), return_index=True\n)\n\n# There are often multiple motifs overlapping one ChIP-seq peak, and a substantial number of peaks without motifs:\n\n# note that counting motifs per peak can also be handled directly with\n# bioframe.count_overlaps but since we re-use df_peaks_motifs below we\n# instead use the pandas operations directly\nmotifs_per_peak = df_peaks_motifs.groupby([\"index_1\"])[\"index_2\"].count().values\n\nplt.hist(motifs_per_peak, np.arange(0, np.max(motifs_per_peak)))\nplt.xlabel(\"number of overlapping motifs per peak\")\nplt.ylabel(\"number of peaks\")\nplt.semilogy()\n\nprint(\n    f\"fraction of peaks without motifs \"\n    f\"{np.round(np.sum(motifs_per_peak == 0) / len(motifs_per_peak), 2)}\"\n)\n\n# ### Assign the strongest motif to each peak\n\n# since idxmax does not currently take NA, fill with -1\ndf_peaks_motifs[\"pval_2\"] = df_peaks_motifs[\"pval_2\"].fillna(-1)\nidxmax_peaks_motifs = (\n    df_peaks_motifs.groupby([\"chrom_1\", \"start_1\", \"end_1\"])[\"pval_2\"].idxmax().values\n)\ndf_peaks_maxmotif = df_peaks_motifs.loc[idxmax_peaks_motifs]\ndf_peaks_maxmotif[\"pval_2\"].replace(-1, np.nan, inplace=True)\n\n# stronger peaks tend to have stronger motifs:\n\nplt.rcParams[\"font.size\"] = 12\ndf_peaks_maxmotif[\"fc_1\"] = df_peaks_maxmotif[\"fc_1\"].values.astype(\"float\")\nplt.scatter(\n    df_peaks_maxmotif[\"fc_1\"].values,\n    df_peaks_maxmotif[\"pval_2\"].values,\n    5,\n    alpha=0.5,\n    lw=0,\n)\nplt.xlabel(\"ENCODE CTCF peak strength, fc\")\nplt.ylabel(\"JASPAR CTCF motif strength \\n (-log10 pval *100)\")\nplt.title(\n    \"corr: \"\n    + str(np.round(df_peaks_maxmotif[\"fc_1\"].corr(df_peaks_maxmotif[\"pval_2\"]), 2))\n);\n\n# We can also ask the reverse question: how many motifs overlap a ChIP-seq peak?\n\ndf_motifs_peaks = bioframe.overlap(\n    ctcf_motifs, ctcf_peaks, how=\"left\", suffixes=(\"_1\", \"_2\")\n)\n\nm = df_motifs_peaks.sort_values(\"pval_1\")\nplt.plot(\n    m[\"pval_1\"].values[::-1],\n    np.cumsum(pd.isnull(m[\"chrom_2\"].values[::-1]) == 0) / np.arange(1, len(m) + 1),\n)\nplt.xlabel(\"pval\")\nplt.ylabel(\"probability motif overlaps a peak\");\n\n# ### filter peaks overlapping blacklisted regions\n#\n# do any of our peaks overlap blacklisted genomic regions?\n\nblacklist = bioframe.read_table(\n    \"https://www.encodeproject.org/files/ENCFF356LFX/@@download/ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz\",\n    schema=\"bed3\",\n)\nblacklist[0:3]\n\n# there appears to be a small spike in the number of peaks close to blacklist regions\n\nclosest_to_blacklist = bioframe.closest(ctcf_peaks, blacklist)\nplt.hist(\n    closest_to_blacklist[\"distance\"].astype(\"Float64\").astype(\"float\"),\n    np.arange(0, 1e4, 100),\n);\n\n# to be safe, let's remove anything +/- 1kb from a blacklisted region\n\n# first let's select the columns we want for our final dataframe of peaks\n# with motifs\ndf_peaks_maxmotif = df_peaks_maxmotif[\n    [\n        \"chrom_1\",\n        \"start_1\",\n        \"end_1\",\n        \"fc_1\",\n        \"chrom_2\",\n        \"start_2\",\n        \"end_2\",\n        \"pval_2\",\n        \"strand_2\",\n    ]\n]\n#  then rename columns for convenience when subtracting\nfor i in df_peaks_maxmotif.keys():\n    if \"_1\" in i:\n        df_peaks_maxmotif.rename(columns={i: i.split(\"_\")[0]}, inplace=True)\n\n# now subtract, expanding the blacklist by 1kb\ndf_peaks_maxmotif_clean = bioframe.subtract(\n    df_peaks_maxmotif, bioframe.expand(blacklist, 1000)\n)\n\n# there it is! we now have a dataframe containing positions of CTCF ChIP peaks, \n# including the strongest motif underlying that peak, and after conservative\n# filtering for proximity to blacklisted   "specification": {
    "task_brief": "# Task: assign the strongest CTCF motif to each CTCF ChIP-seq peak, then blacklist-filter the result\n\n## Objective\n\nFor the CTCF ChIP-seq peak set from HFF cells (ENCODE, assembly GRCh38), assign to every peak the strongest CTCF motif from the JASPAR MA0139.1 track that overlaps it, and then conservatively remove any peak material lying within \u00b11 kb of ENCODE blacklisted genomic regions. The deliverable is a table of the retained peak intervals, each annotated with the peak's fold change and its assigned motif.\n\n## Supplied inputs (read-only; no network access)\n\n1. `/inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz` \u2014 CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (HFF), gzipped narrowPeak, no header. 40587 rows, each with 10 tab-separated fields in order: `chrom, start, end, name, score, strand, fc, -log10p, -log10q, relSummit`. Only `chrom`, `start`, `end` and `fc` are used; `fc` (the 7th field) is a decimal number.\n2. `/inputs/MA0139.1.tsv.gz` \u2014 CTCF motif occurrences (JASPAR profile MA0139.1, hg38 UCSC track), gzipped, tab-separated. Data rows have exactly 7 tab-separated fields in order: `chrom, start, end, name, score, pval, strand`, where `pval` is the motif score expressed as \u2212log10(p-value) \u00d7 100 (an integer value in this file). The file contains 770050 data rows and no header or track-declaration lines; every decompressed line in the supplied file conforms to this schema. A line that does not conform to the 7-field data-row schema (for example a UCSC `track` declaration, should one be present) is not a data record and must be ignored, as must any blank line.\n3. `/inputs/ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz` \u2014 ENCODE blacklist regions, gzipped BED3 (`chrom, start, end`), no header, 910 rows.\n\nAll coordinates are 0-based, half-open `[start, end)` intervals in base pairs on GRCh38/hg38. Chromosomes are matched by exact name string (no aliasing or prefix normalization). Two intervals on the same chromosome overlap if they share at least one base (`start_A < end_B` and `start_B < end_A`); abutting intervals do not overlap.\n\n## Entities, output grain and combination rules\n\n- The output entities are **distinct peak intervals**, not peak records. The peaks file contains 40587 records over 40572 distinct `(chrom, start, end)` intervals; 15 intervals appear in two records each, with **different `fc` values**. Each distinct interval is analyzed and reported as one peak, annotated with the `fc` of the first record of that interval in the peaks file's row order (the file is sorted ascending by `fc`, so this is also the smaller of the two values).\n- A peak interval can be overlapped by zero, one or many motif records (many is common); the assignment rule below selects a single motif or none.\n- Peaks are neither merged nor re-clustered; each distinct interval is handled independently.\n\n## Analysis specification\n\n1. **Motif assignment per peak.** For each distinct peak interval P = (chrom, start, end), find all motif records whose interval overlaps P. The motif assigned to P is the overlapping motif with the largest `pval`; if several motifs tie for the largest `pval` (such ties do occur for some peaks in this dataset), assign the one that appears **earliest in the motif track file's row order**. A peak with no overlapping motif \u2014 or a peak none of whose overlapping motifs has a defined `pval` \u2014 is retained with blank motif fields. (Every `pval` in the supplied motif file is defined.)\n2. **Blacklist filtering, performed after assignment.** Expand every blacklist interval by 1000 bp on each side and take the union of the expanded intervals (equivalently: first merge expanded intervals that overlap or abut one another). Remove from each peak the portions covered by (sharing at least one base with) the removed set, keeping the surviving sub-intervals with start/end coordinates trimmed to the retained portion. A peak entirely covered by expanded blacklist intervals contributes no rows. Motif assignment is performed on the original, untrimmed peak spans; the blacklist step only trims the reported peak coordinates, so a retained row's assigned motif need not overlap the trimmed sub-interval it is reported on.\n\n## Required output\n\nWrite a single file `/outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv`: UTF-8, comma-separated, exactly one header line followed by one data row per retained peak sub-interval, no index column, no additional files. Columns, in exactly this order and with exactly these names:\n\n```\nchrom,start,end,fc,motif_chrom,motif_start,motif_end,motif_pval,motif_strand\n```\n\n- `chrom`, `start`, `end` \u2014 the retained (possibly trimmed) peak sub-interval; integers.\n- `fc` \u2014 the peak's fold-change value, per the entity rule above.\n- `motif_chrom`, `motif_start`, `motif_end` \u2014 the assigned motif's interval; `motif_start` and `motif_end` are integers.\n- `motif_pval` \u2014 the assigned motif's `pval` score (\u2212log10 p \u00d7 100).\n- `motif_strand` \u2014 the assigned motif's strand (`+` or `-`).\n- Motif fields are blank for peaks with no assigned motif.\n- A peak split into several retained pieces appears once per piece, each row carrying the same `fc` and motif annotation.\n\nRow order is free and will not be evaluated. `fc` and `motif_pval` are decimal numbers; any unambiguous decimal representation of the value is acceptable (for example `450` or `450.0`). The analysis is fully deterministic; no randomness is involved.\n\n## Environment and resources\n\nRun offline. Limits: 4 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 600 s wall-clock. Any toolchain is acceptable provided the output meets the specification above; for convenience a Python environment including bioframe 0.8.0 is available, but its use is not required."
  },
  "verifier_seconds": 120
}
